english.title: Driver of a vehicle fail to stop after a road accident
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the driver of a mechanically propelled vehicle namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..) owing to the presence of which on a

(A)_[road,]_
(B)_[public place]_

namely **(..SPECIFY ROAD OR PUBLIC PLACE AND LOCATION..) an accident occurred whereby

(C)_[personal injury]_
(D)_[damage]_

was caused to

(E)_[another person,]_
(F)_[another vehicle,]_

english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(4) of the Road Traffic Act 1988 and Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
driver of mechanically propelled vehicle
an accident occurred causing personal injury/damage
to another person/another vehicle or
animal not in that vehicle/trailer drawn by that vehicle or

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See also offence wording: H103 re: failing to stop and give name and address etc after accident.
(ii) The offence was extended to include 'other public place' by the The Motor Vehicles (Compulsory Insurance) Regulations 2000 - S.I. 726/2000 refers.
(iii) See section 170(8) for the meaning of 'animal'.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed five to ten penalty points.

Discretionary disqualification.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
